S1:10.text: And again Multiplying, ſayth he, wil I multiplie thy ſeed, and it shal not be numbred for the multitude thereof. †

S1:12.text: He shal be a wild man his hand shal be againſt al men, and al mens hands againſt him: and ouer againſt al his bretheren shal he pitch his tents. †

S1:13.text: And she called the name of our Lord that ſpake vnto her Thou the God which haſt ſene me. For she ſaid verily here haue I ſene the backe partes of him that hath ſene me. †

S1:14.text: Therfore she called that wel, the wel of him that liueth and ſeeth me. The ſame is betwen Cadeſſe, and Barad. †

S1:16.text: Eightie and ſixe yeares old was Abram when Agar brought him forth Iſmael.

S1:9.text: And the angel of our Lord ſaid to her Returne to thy to thy miſtreſſe, and humble thy ſelfe vnder her hand. †

S6:10.text: And againe: Multiplying, ſayth he, wil I multiplie thy ſeed, and it ſhal not be num-bred for the multitude therof.

S6:11.text: And againe after that Behold, ſaith he, thou art with child, and thou ſhalt bring forth a ſonne: and thou ſhalt cal his name Iſmael, becauſe the Lord hath heard thine affliction.

S6:12.text: He ſhal be a wild man his hand ſhal be againſt al men, and al mens hands againſt himꝫ and ouer againſt al his brethren ſhal he pitch his tents.

S6:13.text: And ſhe called the name of our Lord that ſpake vnto her: Thou the God which hath ſeen me. For ſhe ſaid: verily here haue I ſeen the backe parts of him that hath ſeen me. Therfore

S6:14.text: Therfore ſhe called that wel, the wel of him that liueth and ſeeth me. The ſame is between Cadeſſe and Barad.

S6:15.text: And Agar brought forth a ſonne to Abram: who called his name Iſmael.

S6:16.text: Eightie and ſixe yeares old was Abram when Agar brought him forth Iſmael.

S6:3.text: ſhe toke Agar the Ægyptian her handmaid tenne yeares after that they firſt dwelled in the land of Chanaan, and gaue her vnto her huſband to wife.

S6:4.text: Who did companie with her, but ſhe perceiuing that ſhe was with child, deſpiſed her miſtreſſe.

S6:5.text: And Sarai ſaid to Abram: Thou doeit vniuſtly againſt me:I gaue my handmaid into thy boſome, who perceiuing her ſelf to be with child, deſpiſeth me. Our Lord iudge between me and thee.

S6:6.text: To whom Abram making anſwer: Behold, ſaith he, thy handmaid is in thine owne hand, vſe her as it pleaſeth thee. When Sarai therfore did afflict her, ſhe ranne away.

S6:7.text: And an Angel of our Lord hauing found her beſide a fountaine of water in the wilderneſſe, which is in the way to Sur in the deſert,

S6:8.text: he ſaid to her: firmament, the handmaid of Sarai whence commeſt thou? and whither goeſt thou who anſwered From the face of Sarai my miſtreſſe doe I flye,

S6:9.text: And the Angel of our Lord ſaid to her Returne to thy miſtreſſe, and humble thy ſelfe vnder her hand.

S9:5.text: And Sarai ſaid to Abram Thou doeſt vniuſtly againſt me: I gaue my handmaid into thy boſome, who perceauing herſelf to be with child, deſpiſeth me. Our Lord iudge betwene me and thee.

S9:6.text: To whom Abram making anſwere: Behold, ſaith he, thy handmaid is in thine owne hand, vſe her as it pleaſeth thee. When Sarai therfore did afflict her, she ranne away. †

S9:9.text: And the angel of our Lord ſaid to her; Returne to thy to thy miſtreſſe, and humble thy ſelfe vnder her hand.
